statement: Margin, which is the binding constraint, comes from time-free knobs inherited from CIFAR-10 or SGD and never re-tuned on this CIFAR-100 Muon recipe. This has been confirmed: head logit scale 2x (E053, +0.44 pp dev) and the BN-bias LR multiplier 64x→32x→16x (E054, E061, about +0.28 pp per halving) raised the dev mean from 0.7534 to 0.7586, and E055-E059 spent that margin on time cuts. Still untried: the remaining SGD-group step sizes, flip and Cutout, NS quality above the current budget, and reallocating steps from early low-res to the late tail.

An airbench-style net (frozen patch-whitening first conv, Dirac init, 64x BN-bias LR, Lookahead, triangular LR, Nesterov SGD at batch 1024, widths 128/384/576 with 3 convs per group, label smoothing 0.3) reaches the target in about 8.5-10 epochs even with TTA banned. That is about 7x fewer epoch-equivalents of compute than the 40-epoch ResNet9 template.
Prediction: the airbench port at 8.5 epochs, lr 9.0, wd 0.012, ls 0.3, no TTA gives 3-seed mean accuracy in [0.750, 0.758] and time <= 10 s on the A100-SXM.

Prediction: because TTA is banned, 8.5 epochs leaves less than 0.3 pp of margin. Going to about 9.5 epochs (or the equivalent extra width) raises 3-seed mean accuracy by >=0.4 pp, to >=0.756, for <=12% more time.

Prediction (noise model): per-seed accuracy std of the airbench port is <=0.35 pp, and re-running the same config changes the 3-seed mean by <=0.2 pp and the time by <=3%. Deltas below these are treated as inconclusive.
Alternating (deterministic, epoch-alternating) horizontal flip is a free gain in sample efficiency over random flip on CIFAR-100, as on CIFAR-10.

Prediction: on the E061 tip at fixed epochs, switching alternating flip to random flip lowers the dev-seed (3-12) mean by 0.05-0.25 pp with time unchanged. The airbench paper gives about 15% effective speedup at 10 epochs, i.e. about 0.15 epoch-equivalents. A drop >0.3 pp or a rise >0.15 pp would contradict the CIFAR-10 transfer.
With 100 classes and short schedules, stronger output regularization (label smoothing ~0.3) helps, while input regularization such as Cutout hurts at <=10 epochs.
Prediction: on the Muon incumbent at a fixed epoch count, label smoothing 0.3 beats 0.2 by >=0.2 pp in 3-seed mean accuracy.
Prediction: adding Cutout (e.g. 8-12 px) at <=10 epochs lowers 3-seed mean accuracy by >=0.2 pp.
On this CIFAR-100 recipe, Nesterov SGD is more time-efficient than Muon, contrary to the CIFAR-10 airbench94_muon result.

Prediction: Muon on conv weights (lr ~0.24, momentum 0.6, 3 NS steps, batch 2000), given the same wall time as the SGD incumbent, ends >=0.3 pp below it. If Muon instead matches SGD accuracy in >=10% less time, A4 is refuted.

Under SGD, wider-and-shorter (768 at -1 epoch) beat 576 (E004). Under Muon, the only test (E008) widened group 3 and cut 0.5 epoch at the same time, at batch 2000, before resizing, graphs and freezing (-0.30 pp). So the width bonus at equal epochs on the current recipe is unmeasured. See the capacity hypothesis for the equal-epoch test.
Prediction: of the configs that reach >=0.753, widths 128/384/448 at ~10 epochs and 128/384/768 at ~7.5 epochs are each within ±5% of the time of 128/384/576 at the matching epoch count.
Skipping low-loss (easy) examples in later epochs, selected from losses computed during training at no extra cost, cuts the number of steps without losing accuracy.
Prediction: dropping the 25% lowest-loss examples in the last half of training cuts train time by >=10%, with 3-seed mean accuracy falling by <=0.2 pp.

Time is mainly set by per-step throughput: how fast each training step runs on the A100 (precision, memory layout, compilation, data pipeline, FLOPs per step), independent of how many steps are needed.
With 4 pinned CPU cores, a CPU-side DataLoader/augmentation pipeline bottlenecks the GPU. Keeping the full uint8 dataset on the GPU, with crop/flip done there, removes the bottleneck.
Prediction: switching the template's data pipeline to a GPU-resident loader with GPU augmentation cuts per-epoch train time by >=30%, with accuracy unchanged within 0.3 pp.
The torch.compile mode (max-autotune vs default) substantially raises step throughput for this net.

Prediction: adding channels_last + fp16 autocast + max-autotune compile (warmed up in build on synthetic data, for every shape used in training) cuts per-epoch time by >=30%, with 3-seed mean accuracy within 0.3 pp.

Progressive resizing (whole-image bilinear downsampling on a 20 -> 24 -> 28 -> 32 px ladder, with only the last ~4 epochs at 32 px) cuts step cost at little accuracy cost. Step cost concentrates in the high-resolution group-1 layers, so early epochs at low resolution are cheap, and the first epochs are insensitive to resolution down to 20 px.

Prediction: on the E021 incumbent (11-ish total epochs, 5 at 24 px then 32 px), a three-stage schedule of about equal thirds at 24/28/32 px, with total epochs adjusted so the 32 px epoch count is cut by >=1, all shapes graphed in build, cuts mean time by >=3%. 3-seed mean stays >=0.755 (checked with 2 salts).

At a score of about 7 s, fixed overhead in the timed region (prepare: data transfer, whitening init; first-iteration costs and recompiles in train) could be cut without touching accuracy. That has been done: prepare is about 0.06 s and there is no first-trial excess. The lever is exhausted (about 1% of time).

Data-dependent init (patch-whitening covariance) and data preparation in prepare can be made cheap. Estimating whitening from a ~5000-image subset and doing one bulk uint8 transfer to the GPU keeps prepare small.

Prediction: computing whitening from 5000 sampled training images instead of all 50k cuts prepare time by >=0.1 s, with 3-seed mean accuracy within 0.2 pp. After optimization, total prepare time is <=0.5 s.

Lazy first-call costs inside the timed train (Muon/Newton-Schulz kernels, allocator growth, optimizer-state creation) add time on the first trial. Warming up the full optimizer step in build can remove them.

Prediction: with drop_last/fixed batch shapes and all shapes warmed up in build, TORCH_LOGS=recompiles shows 0 recompiles during prepare+train. Compared with a config that recompiles, this saves >=0.5 s per trial, and eval returns finite [B,100] logits within 5 s for B in {1, 7, 513, 1024}.

Muon-internal settings (lr, momentum, NS polynomial and steps, schedule shape) inherited from CIFAR-10 are off-optimum for this net. So far the knobs are flat (lr E028, momentum E040) or worse when changed (NS E035, E052, Lookahead/triangle E016). The SGD-group gains (E054, E061) now sit under their own Lvl2.

Prediction (exchange rate under Muon): the Muon incumbent at 8.5 and 9.5 epochs gives an accuracy slope of 0.6-1.2 pp/epoch. The marginal pp/s from this slope becomes the reference for re-scoring E009 and E010.

Prediction: on the Muon incumbent at a fixed epoch count, removing Lookahead and replacing the triangular schedule with linear decay from the start (no warmup) changes 3-seed mean accuracy by >=+0.2 pp, and per-step time does not rise.
Prediction: batch 1536 with Muon lr 0.205 and momentum 0.655 (Hiverge), at the same epoch count, beats batch 2000 / lr 0.24 / momentum 0.6 by >=0.2 pp in 3-seed mean, with <=3% more time.

Prediction (attribution): Nesterov SGD at batch 2000 with 9.0 epochs (lr rescaled airbench-style) lands >=0.4 pp below E007's Muon run (0.7544). If so, E007's gain comes from the optimizer, not from the batch-size change.
Prediction: on E033, ending the linear LR decay at a floor of 5% of peak (Fable's 0.05 floor), with Lookahead kept, raises the 2-salt mean by >=0.15 pp at fixed epochs and time.

source: results:E004 (+19% MACs gave +6% ms/step), E009 (-6% MACs gave -9% ms/step), E010; review
statement: Work removal: backward and forward work that carries little accuracy can be removed. This holds for early-layer backward at high resolution (E029, E033), but conv1 still needs its 28 px updates (E050). Depth floors are reached: group 1 = 2 (E023), group 2 = 2 (E059, a very cheap cut), group 3 = 3 (E062, -0.89 pp). Further removal must come from width or from the step allocation.
Prediction: a torch.profiler breakdown of one incumbent step shows >=40% of GPU time in non-convolution kernels (BN, activation, pooling, elementwise), and most of it in the 32x32 and 16x16 stages.

Prediction: under Muon, cutting group 1 to 2 convs (as in E009) and training at 9.5 epochs gives 3-seed mean >=0.755 at <=8.5 s, which beats the E007 incumbent on time while keeping or improving its margin.

Prediction: the E009 vs E010 ranking (depth cut 0.41 pp/s vs width cut 0.82 pp/s) is within noise. Group 1 at 2 convs and width 112, with epochs added to reach >=0.755, is within 2% of the time of the depth-only cut at matched accuracy.

source: search:github.com/fulcrumresearch/cifar-10-speedrun (CUDA Graph / Optimizer Fusion); github.com/hiverge/cifar10-speedrun (batched NS); results:E007 (~4% Muon overhead)
statement: Python and kernel-launch overhead from the multi-group optimizer step (Muon Newton-Schulz per parameter, Lookahead, separate SGD groups) costs a measurable share of step time that compile flags do not reach. Capturing the train and optimizer steps in a CUDA graph, with foreach-fused updates and Newton-Schulz batched across parameters, removes it.

Prediction: batching Newton-Schulz across conv weights into one call and capturing the full step (forward, backward, Muon, SGD) as a CUDA graph warmed up in build cuts train time by >=3%. 3-seed mean accuracy stays within 0.1 pp, since the change is numerically equivalent.

Prediction: running the full optimizer step (including Muon/Newton-Schulz and optimizer-state allocation) on synthetic data in build, then resetting state in prepare, removes the first trial's ~0.15 s train-time excess. Trial 1's train time comes within 0.05 s of trials 2-3.

Progress is limited by decision and selection noise. The official 3-seed metric is deterministic per code (E046 = E038, E060 = E059), but any code change re-rolls the trajectories. Across 13 recipes, official minus dev-seed mean is a zero-mean residual with σ≈0.2 pp (E048-E063); the earlier '+0.15 pp favourable official seeds' was specific to the E038 family. Combined with a dev-mean SE of about 0.08 pp, an official draw ≥0.753 needs dev ≳0.7558 for P≈0.9 (≳0.7547 for P≈0.8). Repeated knob selection on the same dev seeds 3-12 adds its own winner's curse. Levers: decide on dev means, keep a fresh held-out seed block for de-biasing, and never fish for passing draws.

Noise model: the official 3-seed metric is a deterministic function of the code (E002/E003, E046). The noise that matters is the code- or salt-induced trajectory re-roll. Per-seed std is about 0.28 pp (E046, 10 dev seeds), so a 3-seed mean has SE ≈ 0.16 pp, a config-to-config difference on official seeds ≈ 0.23 pp, and on 10 dev seeds ≈ 0.13 pp (not variance-paired). Deltas under 2 SE (≈0.26 pp on 10 dev seeds) are inconclusive in either direction. Salts and dev seeds are valid replicates; repeat runs are not.

Prediction: re-running the E021 incumbent with 3-4 different internal augmentation/data-order salts (trial seeds fixed) gives a 3-seed-mean spread (max minus min) of 0.15-0.4 pp, i.e. sigma ~0.08-0.2 pp. Deltas below ~2 sigma are then inconclusive.

Averaging weights late in training (an EMA over the last ~1 epoch, with BN statistics re-estimated or the EMA applied to BN buffers) lowers per-seed accuracy variance and slightly raises the mean in this under-trained regime.
Prediction: adding a weight EMA (decay tuned so it covers about the last epoch) to the Muon incumbent lowers per-seed accuracy std by >=30% and does not lower the 3-seed mean, with <=2% added time.

On the resizing recipe, the marginal value of extra training is unresolved. Two single-salt runs showed no gain: E032 (+0.5 epoch at 32 px, -0.06 pp) and E036 (+1 epoch at 20 px, -0.27 pp). Both are confounded, because the warmup fraction, the Lookahead ramp and the whitening-bias window are defined over total steps and move when epochs are added. Each delta is about 1 SE. Whether the recipe is still under-trained (~0.5-1 pp/epoch) or near a plateau decides whether epochs can buy margin.

Prediction: on the E021 recipe at 9.25, 10.25 and 11.25 32-px-equivalent epochs (low-res share fixed), with 2 internal salts per point, the accuracy-vs-time slope is 0.6-1.2 pp/s, and the 9.25 to 10.25 step adds >=0.5 pp. Every per-step cut is then re-scored against this line.

Prediction: a lighter loss filter on E021 (drop the 10-15% lowest-loss examples, only in the last third of training) plus about +0.5 epoch reaches a 3-seed mean >=0.755 at lower time than E021. Equivalently, its pp/s cost sits below the N1a slope. If it does not, H1.6 is refuted.

Prediction: on E021 at batch 1536, scaling the Muon lr by 0.8x and 1.25x (momentum fixed) moves the 3-seed mean by >=0.25 pp in one direction (2 salts each). This means the inherited Hiverge lr is not at the optimum for this net.

FixRes-style mechanism, narrowed: low-res training costs little because the closing 32 px phase mainly re-fits the deeper layers, BN statistics and head to the test resolution, so that phase can be shorter (e.g. 3x28 + 3x32, E037: -0.10 s, -0.08 pp on one draw against a biased baseline). The BN-re-estimation branch is closed: end-of-train re-estimation on clean 32 px images gave no gain (E043 +0.11 pp official; E048 ≈ -0.08 pp net of the pooling cut on dev). Fable's CIFAR-10 champion spends only 3 of 9 epochs at 32 px.

Prediction: in the 24 px phase, step cost per image is lower, so Muon's fixed ~2 ms per step is a larger share. Raising the batch to 2048-3072 in the low-res phase only (Muon lr scaled by sqrt of the batch ratio, separate graph captured in build) cuts low-res phase time by >=8% and total time by >=2%. The 3-seed mean stays within noise (2 salts).

Prediction (resolution-tied regularization): on E021 at fixed epochs, label smoothing ~0.2 and crop translation scaled to 24 px during the low-res phase, with ls 0.3 at 32 px, raises the 3-seed mean by >=0.15 pp (2 salts). That margin would allow ~0.2-0.3 fewer epochs.

Prediction: training the whitening-conv bias only in the first ~1-3 epochs and then stopping backward before the 32x32 whitening stage (a second CUDA graph captured in build) cuts ms/step by >=2% in the later epochs and total time by >=1.5%. The 3-seed mean stays within noise.

Prediction: replacing 3-step Newton-Schulz with AOL (Turbo-Muon) column preconditioning plus 2 NS steps saves about 0.3-0.5 ms/step, cutting train time by >=1%, with the 3-seed mean within noise. Going further to 1 NS step is not viable: E035 lost 1.8 pp, because real momentum-gradient matrices have long tails of small singular values that one step cannot lift.

Winner's curse: draws kept near the bar overstate expected accuracy (the E038 family's kept 0.7546 vs a 16-draw mean of 0.7531). Official seeds 0-2 are not systematically favourable: official minus dev ≈ 0 ± 0.2 pp across E048-E063.

source: review; search:abdullah-athar PR #3 (SXM vs PCIe note)
statement: The local score may not carry over to official judging. The official repo confirms the judge is an A100 80GB PCIe (300 W cap vs 400 W SXM, ~1935 vs 2039 GB/s) with 40 trials; the L40S/50-trial snippet was wrong. Time wins that remove work (steps, pixels, NS iterations, backward passes) should carry over roughly proportionally. Wins under ~2% that depend on kernel scheduling or launch overhead may shrink or reverse.

Mechanism: a power-capped PCIe A100 lowers sustained clocks under the compute-bound conv kernels more than under the launch- or memory-bound parts. Conv-FLOP cuts (resizing, depth cuts) therefore carry over at least proportionally, while overhead cuts (CUDA graphs, fused updates) carry over proportionally less. Rank candidate changes by work removed when local deltas are within ~2%.
The recipe's accuracy is capped near 75.3% by model capacity and the regularization balance, not by step count or optimizer settings.

Group-3 capacity buys accuracy at equal epochs, but at about 1 pp/s under the current Muon + resize + freeze recipe: 768 gave +0.4 pp on one draw for +10% time (E044), and 640 gave +0.19 pp dev for +2.9% time (E051). Both include Newton-Schulz cost growth. That is no better than an epoch line not re-measured since E014. Cheaper capacity, if any, is in group 2 (16→8 px), where a depth-for-width trade could add margin and remove time at once.
Prediction: on E033 at equal epochs and schedule, group 3 at 768 (instead of 576) raises the 2-salt mean by >=0.3 pp for <=+5% time. That buys margin at a better rate than the epoch line.
Prediction: on E033 at equal epochs, group 2 at 512 (instead of 384) raises the 2-salt mean by >=0.25 pp for <=+6% time. The 16x16-to-8x8 group-2 layers are the next-cheapest capacity after group 3.

Accuracy depends on how many optimizer steps fall at peak and decaying LR, and where they sit relative to the schedule anchors (warmup fraction, Lookahead alpha ramp, whitening-bias window, resolution boundaries), not on epochs or pixels as such. This explains why adding low-res steps hurt (E036), removing early steps hurt (E031), and adding a 32 px tail did nothing (E032).

Prediction: on the pooling-cut base, re-run E036's extra 20 px epoch with warmup, Lookahead ramp and whitening-bias window fixed in absolute steps (same code path as H1.8.2). On dev seeds 3-12 the mean is ≥0.15 pp above the base's dev mean, where E036 lost 0.27 pp. If anchoring alone recovers the loss, the resolution-ladder decisions (E025, E030, E037), which all moved the anchors implicitly, need re-checking.

Prediction (clean slope test, highest priority): on the pooling-cut base, add 1.5 full-res epochs with warmup length, Lookahead ramp and whitening-bias window fixed in absolute steps. Evaluated on dev seeds 3-12, this raises the mean by ≥0.5 pp for about +1.2 s (≈0.4 pp/s or better). If the gain is <0.2 pp, the recipe is near a plateau and H6 gains support. The result replaces the E014-era exchange rate used to score every capacity and time trade.

Kernel efficiency: non-conv kernels are about 23% of fwd+bwd GPU time (E018 profile). Some is avoidable without removing learning: the AdaptiveMaxPool2d(1) backward (slow atomic kernel), train-mode BN on frozen blocks, and GELU at high resolution. Replacing them with cheaper equivalents cuts ms/step at every resolution.
Prediction: replacing AdaptiveMaxPool2d(1) in the head with x.flatten(2).amax(2) (numerically identical) cuts mean time by >=1% on E033. Accuracy is bit-identical or within 0.05 pp.

Prediction: in E033's 32 px phase, running the frozen group-1 block's BN in eval mode (or folding it into its conv as a fixed affine) cuts mean time by >=1%. The 2-salt mean stays within 0.1 pp of 0.7525.

Prediction: training the whitening bias for only ~0.2 epoch, as Fable and Hiverge do, then detaching the whitening output in every phase including 20/24 px, cuts mean time by >=2% vs E033. The 2-salt mean stays within 0.1 pp (E029 found 5 vs 3 epochs of bias training neutral).

Prediction: extending E033's freeze of the first group-1 conv block to the 28 px phase cuts mean time by >=1.5%, with the 2-salt mean within 0.1 pp. Keep it only when stacked on a base whose 2-salt mean is >=0.754.

Prediction: weight renormalization in Muon every k steps (k rising from 2 to 17 over training, as in Hiverge and Fable) instead of every step cuts mean time by >=0.5%, with the 2-salt mean within 0.1 pp. This is an overhead-type cut, so treat it as provisional under H5.

Prediction: capturing the whole training run (all phases, with precomputed per-step scalars) as one CUDA graph, instead of one step graph per resolution, cuts mean time by >=1% on E033 with identical numerics. Most of the gain is launch overhead and may not transfer to the judge (H5.1).
Prediction: on E033, Muon momentum 0.75 vs 0.655 (and 0.6) moves the 2-salt mean by >=0.2 pp in one direction. Momentum has never been varied on this net.

Prediction (mechanism behind E028's flat lr): with per-step weight renorm and Lookahead, the per-layer angular change per 5-step Lookahead cycle differs by <10% between lr 0.205 and 0.256. The lr is then not an effective knob, and the update-magnitude target (Fable schedules 0.50 -> 0.079) is the real one.

Prediction: replacing the 2 post-AOL fixed quintic NS steps with Polar Express minimax coefficients recomputed for num_iters=2 (not the first 2 entries of the 10-step schedule), with the lower bound l set from the smallest post-AOL singular values measured on captured real gradients, raises the 2-draw mean by >=0.15 pp on the tip at equal cost. It does so by lifting small singular values better (the factor E035 identified as binding).

Prediction: E016's -0.52 pp is mostly due to Lookahead. On E033, removing only the triangle warmup (linear decay from peak, Lookahead kept) moves the 2-salt mean by <0.15 pp. Removing only Lookahead costs >=0.3 pp.

Prediction: on E033 at fixed epochs, label smoothing 0.4 (vs 0.3) raises the 2-salt mean by >=0.15 pp. With 100 classes, more smoothing helps (0.3 >= 0.2 in E012), and the upward direction is untested.
Prediction: scaling the head output (logit scale, set for 100 classes and never swept) by 0.5x or 2x on E033 moves the 2-salt mean by >=0.15 pp in one direction, with time unchanged.

Prediction: adding GPU-side per-image brightness/contrast jitter (±0.14 / ±0.13, Hiverge/Fable) to E033 changes the 2-salt mean by >=0.15 pp. The sign is uncertain: it helps on CIFAR-10 at about 8 epochs, while H1.3 expects input regularization to hurt at short schedules on CIFAR-100.

Prediction: evaluating the E033 recipe on dev seeds 3-12, outside the official command, gives a 10-seed mean in [0.7500, 0.7530] (below its kept 0.7531) and a per-seed std of 0.1-0.4 pp. If the mean is <0.7525, no further time cut is kept until a margin-adding change passes with 2 salts.

source: review; results:E002, E003, E018, E020, E043
statement: Variance source: re-rolls on the official metric come almost entirely from code- and salt-dependent trajectory changes, which are deterministic per process. Run-to-run GPU nondeterminism (cuDNN benchmark or max-autotune kernel picks, per the PyTorch randomness docs) happens only occasionally (E043 smoke vs official) and is not routine (E046 = E038 bit-identical). The per-seed std drop from 0.40 to 0.08 pp was a small-sample artefact, not a freezing effect.

Prediction: running the E038 tip unchanged at salt 0 twice in separate processes gives bit-identical per-seed accuracies. If so, E043's smoke/official mismatch came from E043's own code or the smoke path, and salts remain the correct replicate. If the runs differ by >=0.05 pp on any seed, run-to-run noise is real: repeats and salts are equivalent draws, and repeated official runs of identical code must not be used for selection.

Prediction (margin accounting): a second, pre-registered draw of the E024 recipe (before the 28 px and 20 px rungs, detach and freeze) gives a 2-draw mean >=0.755. That would mean the E025-E033 cuts together cost ~0.25-0.3 pp of expected accuracy, and reverting the single most costly cut (likely the 28 px rung) is a cheaper margin source than adding capacity. A mean <0.7535 means those cuts were free and the margin was never there.

Orthogonalization quality limits final accuracy. E035 showed that losing small-singular-value lift costs 1.8 pp, and the recipe may sit on a gentler slope of the same curve with AOL + 2 NS steps. If so, the optimizer, not step count, sets solution quality, which would also explain why extra epochs (E032, E036) did not help.

Prediction: on the tip at fixed epochs, a third NS step (AOL + 3) raises the 2-draw mean by >=0.2 pp for ~+1-1.5% time. A gain <0.1 pp means 2 steps already saturate orthogonalization quality, and H1.7.9 should be deprioritized.

Prediction: group 3 at 640 (instead of 576), at equal epochs on the tip, costs <=+4% ms/step in a microbenchmark and raises the 2-draw mean by >=0.2 pp. Stacked with the -0.19 s pooling cut, the result is net faster than 6.68 s with a 2-draw mean >=0.754.

Prediction (work removal in group 2): cutting group 2 from 3 convs to 2 (2/2/3) cuts mean time by >=4%. The 2-draw mean drops by <=0.3 pp, so it beats the epoch line if paired with a margin source. Group-1 depth showed strongly diminishing returns (E009 -0.29 pp, E023 -1.4 pp), so a single group-2 cut is the untested next candidate.

Prediction: training the whitening bias for ~1 epoch (between E045's 8 steps, which failed, and E029's 3 epochs, which were neutral), then detaching the whitening output in every phase including 20/24 px, cuts mean time by >=1.5%. The 2-draw mean stays within 0.1 pp of the tip family. airbench94_muon uses 3 epochs, Hiverge 0.2 epoch, so the useful window is recipe-dependent.

Prediction: adding NorMuon-style per-row (per output filter) normalization after orthogonalization raises the 2-draw mean by >=0.15 pp at <=1% added time. Muon's orthogonalized updates have uneven per-neuron norms, which the per-step weight renorm does not equalize within a step.

Prediction: under per-step weight renormalization, decoupled weight decay on Muon weights is a dead knob, since the renorm undoes the rescaling (airbench94_muon applies no wd to Muon weights). The live, never-swept knobs are the SGD-group weight decay, the SGD-group momentum (Hiverge uses 0.825) and the 64x BN-bias LR multiplier. Scaling the BN-bias LR multiplier or the SGD-group wd by 0.5x or 2x on the pooling-cut base moves the dev-seed mean by ≥0.2 pp in one direction, with time unchanged.

Equivalent cuts (identical forward/backward up to ties and rounding) leave expected accuracy unchanged, but each one re-rolls the official draw. Run an equivalent cut officially only when the base's dev mean implies P(official ≥0.753) ≳0.85 (dev ≳0.7555, with official − dev σ≈0.2 pp), and never re-submit equivalent variants to fish for a pass.

The ~75.3% ceiling is a fitting limit, not a generalization-gap limit. At the end of the 11-epoch recipe (ls 0.3-0.4, light augmentation), the net under-fits the training set, so margin comes from more effective steps or capacity rather than from regularization or augmentation changes. If instead the train-test gap is large, the regularization axis (flip, Cutout, smoothing form, jitter) is the lever. No hypothesis has yet measured train fit.

Mechanism: with Muon at ~350 steps and label smoothing, the last-epoch training loss is dominated by under-fit hard and fine-grained classes, not by memorization. Capacity (group-3 768/640) and extra anchor-fixed steps should therefore raise un-augmented train accuracy at least as much as test accuracy, and the train-test gap should stay moderate.
Prediction (dev-only diagnostic): un-augmented top-1 on a fixed 10k training subset is in [0.82, 0.92] for the tip, with a train-test gap ≤15 pp. Train accuracy ≥0.95 refutes N1.

Prediction: replacing uniform label smoothing with online label smoothing on the pooling-cut base raises the dev-seed (3-12) mean by ≥0.15 pp at ≤0.5% added time. Online label smoothing keeps a 100x100 per-class soft-label buffer, built from correct-sample predictions in the previous epoch, updated by scatter-add inside the graph and reset in prepare, with loss 0.5·CE(hard) + 0.5·CE(soft) and uniform ls in epoch 1. Its gain at 11 epochs is likely well under the 1.1 pp reported on long schedules.

Prediction (conditional on RULES.md allowing CIFAR-100 coarse labels as part of the training set; check before any run): hierarchical label smoothing, which spreads the smoothing mass mostly within the true superclass, raises the dev-seed mean by ≥0.15 pp at zero time cost versus uniform ls.

Prediction (work removal, numerically near-equivalent): if E024's AOL implementation computes X^T X for the column scaling and then recomputes the Gram in the first NS step, reusing it as A1 = sA0s (Turbo-Muon Algorithm 2) removes one large matmul per parameter per step. That cuts Muon time by ≥0.15 ms/step and total time by ≥0.5%, with the dev-seed mean within 0.1 pp. Check the code first; if the reuse is already in place, close this.

Prediction: a 2-iteration Gram Newton-Schulz (iterate on the n×n Gram, apply the polynomial to X once; α≈9 for our conv matrices) in fp16 with a 1.05 safety factor is numerically stable on captured real momentum gradients: max singular-value error ≤0.05 relative to standard AOL+2. It cuts Muon GPU time by ≥30% (≈0.1-0.2 s per trial) with the dev-seed mean within 0.1 pp. Instability in the offline check refutes it without an official run.

source: review; results:E042 (hidden 2.8% atomic pooling kernel), E047
statement: Prediction: a fresh per-phase torch.profiler capture of the current tip (top-20 kernels by self time, plus un-graphed per-epoch augmentation, resize and Lookahead work) finds non-fused, atomic or scatter kernels and un-graphed per-epoch work totalling ≥3% of train time. Candidates are the in-group MaxPool2d backward, indexing in crop/flip/interpolate and Lookahead copies. Removing the largest of them cuts total time by ≥1% with identical numerics.

Prediction (depth-for-width in group 2): replacing group 2's 3 convs at 384 with 2 convs at 512 (head and group-3 input adjusted), after a ms/step microbenchmark on the current recipe, gives ≤ -2% ms/step and a dev-seed mean within -0.1 pp or better of the pooling-cut base. That would add margin per second at once, which single-axis cuts (H2.4.7, H6.1.2) cannot.

Prediction (pre-registered stacking forecast): the stack of 640 + pooling cut + 2-epoch bias window + 28 px tail shift gives a dev-seed (3-12) mean in [0.7520, 0.7540] at 6.50-6.56 s, so P(official ≥ 0.753) ≈ 0.5. It is therefore not run officially until another +0.1-0.2 pp of time-free margin is confirmed on dev seeds. A dev mean ≥0.7545 refutes this forecast and licenses the official run.

Prediction: matching both reference recipes' BN settings (BN weight frozen at 1, eps 1e-12; airbench94_muon and Hiverge) on the pooling-cut base, if the port differs, leaves the dev-seed mean within ±0.1 pp or raises it, and cuts time by ≥0.3% by dropping the BN-weight gradient and optimizer group. Check the code first; close if already matched.

source: review; results:E053, E054, E061; search:airbench94_muon.py, hiverge cifar10_speedrun.py
statement: After the Muon switch, the effective step sizes and temperature of the parameters left on SGD (BN biases, whitening bias, head weights through the logit scale and head lr, SGD-group momentum) are mis-scaled. Both large margin gains since E030 (head scale E053, BN-bias multiplier E054/E061) came from this group, and the BN-bias optimum is not yet bracketed. In both Muon references the bias lr is about 10-13x below the head lr.

Prediction: on the E061 tip, BN-bias multiplier 8x (vs 16x) raises the dev-seed (3-12) mean by ≥0.15 pp with time unchanged. If it does, try 4x. If dev falls ≥0.15 pp, 16x brackets the optimum. Log the absolute bias:head lr ratio; the references sit at about 1:10-1:13.

Prediction: at fixed head scale 2x on the E061 tip, scaling the head lr by 0.5x or 2x moves the dev mean by ≥0.15 pp in one direction. Under Agarwala et al., the effective head lr scales as lr·β², so E053's 2x scale also quadrupled the effective head lr and the two knobs need separating.

Prediction: at the new BN-bias 16x setting, re-sweeping head scale (1.5x and 3x vs 2x) moves the dev mean by ≥0.15 pp in one direction, because both knobs act through the logits and the 2x optimum was found at 64x/32x.
Prediction: SGD-group momentum 0.825 (Hiverge) instead of the inherited airbench value changes the dev mean by ≥0.15 pp, with time unchanged. The sign is uncertain.

Accuracy is set mainly by the late, high-resolution, low-LR steps. Early low-res epochs are saturated (adding one cost 0.27 pp in E036 and 0.18 pp in E063, even with anchors fixed), a 32 px epoch moved to 28 px costs little (E056), and trimming the 32 px tail costs about 0.67 pp/s (E058, 3→2.5 epochs). So time can be removed early and, if needed, spent in the tail.
Prediction: on the E061 tip, dropping one 24 px epoch (2x20+2x24+3x28+2.5x32) with LR warmup and the Lookahead ramp anchored in absolute steps saves ≥0.3 s and costs <0.1 pp dev mean.
Prediction: re-spending the time saved by N_ALLOC.1 on +0.5 epoch at 32 px (net about equal time to E061) raises the dev mean by ≥0.15 pp over E061. This is a net-positive reallocation.

Step cost under the current recipe is roughly MAC-proportional and dominated by the group-2/3 entry convs (128→384 at 16x16, 384→576 at 8x8) plus Newton-Schulz cost per weight shape, not by group 1. E059's 2.2 ms/step for one 8x8 conv and E044's +10% for group-3 768 both fit this. Width cuts in groups 2/3, never tried under Muon, are the remaining work-removal lever now that the depth floors are reached.
Prediction: a per-layer, per-phase profiler capture of the E061 tip shows the group-2 and group-3 entry convs (fwd+bwd) taking ≥45% of conv GPU time, and group 1 (after freezing and detaching) ≤20%.
Prediction: group-2 width 384→320 on the E061 tip (microbenchmark first) cuts mean time by ≥5% at a dev-mean cost of ≤0.2 pp, i.e. ≤0.7 pp/s, at or better than the 32 px tail rate.
Prediction: group-3 width 576→512 on the E061 tip cuts mean time by ≥4% at a dev-mean cost of ≤0.25 pp. E051 measured the opposite step (+64 channels) at +0.19 pp for about +2.9% time.

Muon accuracy is steeply sensitive to orthogonalization quality at the current budget: 1 NS step cost 1.8 pp (E035) and a truncated Polar Express cost 2.1 pp (E052). AOL + 2 fixed quintic steps may therefore sit below saturation, so one more step could buy margin.
Prediction: on the E061 tip at fixed epochs, AOL + 3 NS steps raises the dev mean by ≥0.2 pp for ≤+2% time. A gain under 0.1 pp means 2 steps already saturate quality.

source: search:arxiv.org/pdf/2202.08835 (Smith, cyclical training); legacy airbench96.py; results:E060
statement: Prediction (phase-scoped input regularization): on the E061 tip, Cutout 8 px applied only in the 24/28 px phases (20 px and the 32 px tail left clean) changes the dev mean by ≥0.15 pp. A null result (|Δ|<0.1 pp), together with a null flip test (H1.2.1), means input regularization is not the binding axis despite the 21 pp train-test gap.

Prediction: dev seeds 3-12 have been used for about 6 selection decisions. Evaluating the E061 tip once on fresh held-out seeds 13-22 (kept out of all later selection) gives a mean 0.05-0.2 pp below its dev mean of 0.7586, with per-seed std 0.2-0.3 pp, not E061's 0.13.
